added: post-hoc diagnostic, run after the three preregistered repeats
why: Experiments 74 and 77 reported fold-4 OCF 16.126 and 15.889 for mice1 with the same base model. The three preregistered repeats here were bit-identical (std = 0), so training is deterministic and the discrepancy had to come from the scoring path.

control.design: train the base model once per mouse; compute the official OCF twice on the same logits, once with raw scores and once after per-row z-scoring, with Hungarian assignment in both cases

finding: A per-row monotone affine rescaling of identical scores changes the official OCF by 0.14-0.24. The 2748 x 2748 assignment is nearly degenerate at this signal level, so the solver can return different assignments that are numerically tied in total score.
implications: training is deterministic under a fixed seed; run-to-run training noise is not the limiting factor
the OCF has an irreducible assignment-arbitrariness floor of roughly 0.25 at this signal level
any single-run OCF difference below about 0.25 is not interpretable, including small historical gains
the Task 3 multi-seed gain (+0.6996, experiment 75) was measured with one fixed scoring path and also raised top1, so it remains above this floor, but its magnitude is uncertain by the same order
v5 production scores are computed after row-z fusion, which fixes one arbitrary convention; changing score scaling changes the shipped OCF without changing the model
recommendation: canonicalise scores (always row-z, or a deterministic tie-break) before Hungarian in every experiment and in production, and treat sub-0.3 OCF differences as unresolved unless they repeat across mice and folds
